decisiveClaims.text: Concurrent demand overlap alone does not prove acute/chronic interference or necessity; endpoint, actual dose, timing, context and response matter.

confidence.rationale: Chronic and acute reviews show outcome- and protocol-dependent results; exact individual response remains unknown.

counterevidence: R2-S05: explosive-strength versus maximal-strength findings differ
R2-S06: some acute outcomes unchanged, performance reporting heterogeneous
decisiveClaims.population: Healthy adults/runners in study protocols; not clinical
decisiveClaims.limits: No universal minimum hours, automatic deletion of Strength or global fatigue score.

decisiveClaims.text: Endurance taper evidence supports a direction of lower volume retaining relevant intensity, with population/protocol limits.

confidence.rationale: Applicable endurance systematic synthesis; recreational hybrid combined recipe indirect.

counterevidence: R2-S08: few RCTs, mostly male trained endurance cohorts and heterogeneous responses
decisiveClaims.population: Endurance study populations; transfer to bounded familiar recreational hybrid is conditional
decisiveClaims.limits: Pooled subgroup percentages not individual taper law; exact seven-day week is DECIDED composition.

decisiveClaims.text: The exact1x5 three-machine exposure is not proven to preserve every strength adaptation through a hybrid event week.

confidence.rationale: No direct combined exact protocol trial found in bounded search; indirect narrative maintenance evidence cannot supply it.

counterevidence: Maintenance studies in mostly general populations and different prescriptions cannot establish hybrid1x5 optimality.
decisiveClaims.limits: Not used as decisive positive claim. Protocol may preserve intent only; if preservation of adaptation is necessary, dependent decision remains unsupported.

decisiveClaims.text: CS, LT2, MLSS, race pace and familiar field-session targets must remain distinct, with method-specific calibration and comparison.

confidence.rationale: Current open scoping review directly rejects interchangeability; measurement protocols/context vary.
